claim_text: False news sites in France and Italy had average monthly reach of over 3.5%
method: Comscore audience panel data; monthly reach of false-news vs mainstream news sites in France and Italy

claim_text: None of the false news outlets reached more than one in 20 readers monthly
method: Comscore panel; monthly reach of top false-news sites compared with established outlets (Le Figaro 22.3%, La Repubblica 50.9%)

claim_text: 58% worldwide worried about what is real and fake online concerning news
method: Digital News Report 2025; YouGov online survey across ~48 markets, self-reported concern

claim_text: About 25% of US midterm election content shared on Twitter classified as junk news
method: ComProp/DemTech; classification of links shared in election-related tweets, junk vs professional news

claim_text: Junk news not prevalent on Twitter but more shared and liked on Facebook
method: DemTech multilingual study of European elections; share of junk vs professional news links across platforms

claim_text: US adults on average saw and remembered 1.14 fake stories before 2016 election
method: Gallup/Knight survey paired with recall of specific fabricated stories before 2016 US election

claim_text: Approximately one in four visited a fake news website Oct 7-Nov 14 2016
method: Web-traffic panel; share of individuals who visited at least one fake-news website during 2016 campaign window

claim_text: Almost 6 in 10 visits to fake news websites came from 10% with most conservative diets
method: Survey responses linked to individual web-traffic histories; concentration of fake-news visits among heaviest consumers

claim_text: About a quarter (23%) of US adults say they have shared a fake political news story
method: Pew nationally representative survey; self-reported sharing of fabricated political news online
